note: scaling_study.py originally seeded per-epoch crop positions with Python's builtin hash() on a tuple containing strings, which is randomised per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED) -- the same bug class found and fixed in msnsd_validate.py earlier in this project. Fixed here to use a hashlib-based deterministic seed (det_crop_seed). The numbers below are BOTH runs at size=32, everything else identical, to quantify the run-to-run noise this class of bug (and ordinary training-run variance) introduces.
implication: This ~0.4 dB run-to-run spread is comparable to or larger than the differences reported among the 32-150 clip conditions in the main results (scaling_results.json), which are all single-seed runs. The paper (Limitations paragraph) is worded accordingly: only the coarse conclusion (very little data is clearly worse) is supported; the exact shape of the curve from 32 to 150 clips is not distinguishable from run-to-run noise with n=1 seed per size.
sizes_16_64_100_150_status: generated with the original (buggy, non-deterministic) hash-based seeding; not yet regenerated with the fix due to compute budget. A fresh run of the current (fixed) script will reproduce the size=32 condition's numbers exactly, but will NOT exactly reproduce the other four sizes' numbers reported in the paper -- expect differences of a similar order (~0.3-0.5 dB) to the size=32 case above, not a change in the qualitative conclusion.
